evidence.note: Runs run_tests.sh and python kernel.py after changes, checking both correctness and cycle count (e.g. reports scratch usage 748/1536 at step 10, 5597 cycles at 21) — the anchor-5 baseline loop.
Isolates a sub-computation by testing with 1 round (1069 cycles, works) then 16 rounds (fails), localizing the index-wrapping bug — a sub-computation isolation trait from anchor 8.
Runs py_compile as an independent pre-check before executing — building slightly tighter feedback than just the full test.
Counts actual instruction count to attribute where cycles go — a form of per-transformation cycle attribution, but done only sporadically.

Relies on run_tests.sh to catch scratch overflow and a regression (tree opt worsened 2826->2999), then reverts — verification catches regressions but only via the provided harness, not independent differential testing vs the reference.

reasoning: The agent consistently ran the provided test after meaningful changes and checked both correctness and cycle count (anchor 5), and added several tighter checks beyond it — isolating behavior by reducing rounds, counting instructions for cycle attribution, compile pre-checks, and scratch-limit monitoring. But it never built genuine differential testing against the reference on custom/edge inputs, nor an independent bundle slot-limit checker, relying on the simulator/harness to surface violations. That mix of anchor-5 baseline plus a few sporadic anchor-8 traits, without a systematic layered harness, places it at a 6.
